articles.body:
Alexis Mac Allister Contract Situation Raises January Questions for Liverpool

Liverpool might have expected the closing of the transfer window to bring a little calm. Instead, Alexis Mac Allister's contract situation has ensured that January already feels uncomfortably close.

Speaking alongside Trev Downey on an Anfield Index podcast, Dave Davis examined Mac Allister's comments about his Liverpool future and the consequences they could have when the transfer market reopens. The midfielder has two years remaining on his contract, but his public admission that he was disappointed not to receive a new deal has changed the conversation.

Davis highlighted Mac Allister's words: "It makes me sad I didn't get a new deal, but there is still time. I will give 100% until the last day I am here. We will see what happens."

For Liverpool, those comments have created questions that could persist all the way to January.

Mac Allister Comments Put Liverpool Under Scrutiny

Davis was particularly struck by Mac Allister's repeated expressions of disappointment and the midfielder's explanation that discussions had taken place through his representative rather than directly with him.

Mac Allister said: "There wasn't any direct conversation with me. It was with my agent. I don't want to say things that were never said, but what I got from my agent is they weren't in a position to renew me."

Davis picked out that particular wording, describing "weren't in a position to renew me" as an "interesting choice of phrase".

Mac Allister also referenced teammates who had received new contracts, saying: "I see Dominic and Ryan renewing their contracts and that makes me happy as they deserve it. But at the same time, it makes me sad as I do get mine. But there is still time."

For Davis, the timing created another issue, coming immediately before Andoni Iraola's first Champions League match as Liverpool head coach.

January Could Become Crucial for Liverpool

The most significant part of the discussion concerned what happens next.

Davis believes Mac Allister's contractual position could affect Liverpool's negotiating strength if another club makes an approach in January.

"I don't see how this helps at all cuz you're going to have a player who's going to have 18 months left on his deal in January," Davis said.

He then outlined the negotiating problem Liverpool could encounter, suggesting interested clubs could use Mac Allister's public comments and remaining contract length to reduce their offers.

Davis illustrated the point with a hypothetical example, explicitly stressing that he was inventing the figures: "We might have bid 65 million in the summer. Let's call it 45 now because that's what they can do."

His conclusion was clear: "I don't see how this Liverpool help helps us in any way in that sense."

Camara Conversation Returns to Foreground

Another name inevitably entered the discussion, Lamine Camara.

Davis referred to continuing reports surrounding Liverpool's interest in Camara and connected that discussion with the uncertainty around Mac Allister.

"Mac Allister out, Camara in. It almost feels like that's been thrown right to the forefront again, doesn't it?" he said. "And we'll be talking about this all the way to January."

Downey agreed that the situation had become complicated, while identifying the most positive possible outcome as Mac Allister rediscovering his best form and eventually earning another Liverpool contract.

Downey said: "The best case scenario here is that we get a rejuvenated Mac Allister who is actually being spoken about as a candidate for a new contract."

Davis also questioned whether a lucrative new contract would ultimately fit Liverpool's plans, particularly given Mac Allister's age relative to the club's other midfielders and the wider wage structure.

Whatever Liverpool decide, Davis believes the events surrounding Mac Allister have created an awkward business situation.

"Either way, whichever way we dress up or play this scenario, I'm not sure today was a good day for Liverpool in a business sense."

That is where Liverpool now find themselves. Mac Allister has publicly emphasised his love for the club and promised to give "100% until the last day" he remains there. His contract situation, however, is now firmly part of the discussion.

The summer window has barely disappeared from view, yet Liverpool already have another significant question waiting for them as January approaches.

articles.title: Pakistan all out for 133 in third Test vs England after squad changes
articles.summary: England’s pacers cleaned up Pakistan in 34 overs after the visitors’ top five batters failed to score double figures.
articles.body:
Pakistan have claimed another unwelcome record on their cricket tour of England, becoming the first team to have their top five batters dismissed for nine or fewer runs in the first innings, as the visitors were dismissed for 133 in the first innings of the third Test in Birmingham.

Babar Azam’s team included four new faces, including three debutants, after being sent in to bat by Joe Root’s England on an overcast morning at Edgbaston cricket ground on Wednesday.

The visitors entered the match having lost the series 2-0 and faced growing criticism of both their on-field performances and off-field decisions.

Pakistan sent home seven players and sacked both head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and assistant Umar Gul after losing the second Test by 194 runs at Lord’s cricket ground in London. England won the first Test by an innings and 103 runs at Headingley, Leeds, earlier in August.

Neither the new names nor the old guard were able to change the team’s fortunes, as England’s pacers tore through the top order to leave Pakistan reeling at 48-5 by the time captain Babar was dismissed in the 15th over.

Middle-order batter Saud Shakeel offered some resistance with an innings of 43 runs, while a debutant bowler survived the fast-bowling onslaught for 11 balls. Pakistan’s standout bowler Mohammad Abbas was the third player to score in double figures when he scored 21 off 36 balls before his dismissal wrapped up Pakistan’s innings in 33 overs and five balls.

All 10 Pakistan wickets were claimed by pace bowlers, led by Josh Tongue’s 4-42, which included the wickets of Babar and Saud.

Ollie Robinson, player of the match in the first Test, took 3-15, and Jofra Archer claimed 3-25 to end Pakistan’s ordeal.

articles.summary: The Washington Capitals are celebrating the United States' semiquincentennial with a specialty jersey.
articles.body:
The Washington Capitals are celebrating the United States' semiquincentennial with a specialty jersey.

The Caps shared on Wednesday a first look at the jersey, signed versions of which will be auctioned to benefit a nonprofit supporting children in military families.

Trades That Could Happen Before Training Camp

The jersey was designed by two veterans and features six stars on the front in representation of the United States' six military branches, according to the team.

The flag inside the eagle was "inspired by Revolutionary-era printmaking traditions," while the gold accents are an homage to "military ceremonial uniforms," the team reported.

The jersey features American landmarks including the silhouette of the Capitol Building in front of the crest, the Washington Monument on the right shoulder patch and the Statue of Liberty's torch on the left shoulder patch.

The patches also feature the phrase "We the People" and the year 1776 in honor of the signing of the Declaration of Independence.

The auction featuring the jerseys begins Tuesday, Oct. 16 and runs through Thursday, Oct. 15.

Bidding for a specialty jerseys signed by members of the 2026-27 Capitals will begin at $300, while bidding for individual player jerseys will start at $250 each.

This won't be the only specialty jersey the Capitals unveil this season. Fanatics announced last month all 32 NHL franchises are set to debut Hometown Remix looks during the 2026-27 campaign.

Icethetics reported in May the Capitals' look is expected to include the shade of blue used in the team's 1990s "Screaming Eagle" jersey.

The Capitals are preparing to open training camp Sept. 17 before starting the preseason Sept. 20.

Alex Ovechkin is set to open his 22nd NHL season Oct. 2 with a road game against the defending Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes before returning to D.C. for an Oct. 7 home opener against the Pittsburgh Penguins.

articles.title: WWE Rumors on Bayley's Contract, Johnny Gargano's Push and Jordynne Grace's Return
articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.

Conflicting Reports on Bayley's WWE Contractual Status

Following Bayley's return to WWE programming during Monday night's episode of Raw, conflicting reports emerged regarding where she stands with the company.

Dave Meltzer of Wrestling Observer Radio (h/t Subhojeet Mukherjee of Ringside News) initially reported that Bayley had signed a new contract with WWE.

However, Mike Johnson of PWInsider.com (h/t WrestlePurists ) followed up by reporting that Bayley had not signed a new deal and was still working under her existing one.

It isn't definitely known how much time was or is left on Bayley's contract, but Bryan Alvarez of Wrestling Observer Live (h/t WrestlingInc.com's Julien D'Alessandro ) reported last month that Bayley was believed to be under contract until January.

Rumors and speculation regarding Bayley's pro wrestling future have run rampant recently, especially after she was seemingly written off WWE programming following a loss to Lyra Valkyria at Saturday Night's Main Event on July 18.

On Monday's episode of Raw, Bayley resurfaced and cost Valkyria her Money in the Bank qualifying match, which was won by Sol Ruca.

According to Fightful Select (h/t Geno Mrosko of Cageside Seats), AEW has not yet been informed about Bayley potentially re-signing with WWE, and the promotion had "high hopes" about making a run at Bayley and potentially signing her should she become a free agent.

As of now, there appears to be a great deal of confusion regarding whether Bayley has made a long-term commitment to WWE, or if she may be available in four months.

Whatever the case, Bayley is back on WWE TV, which figures to give the Raw women's division a significant shot in the arm.

Johnny Gargano is reportedly ticketed for more television time following his return to the ring last week on SmackDown.

According to Fightful Select (h/t Mrosko ), WWE is planning to feature Gargano more prominently on the blue brand moving forward.

For months, Gargano exclusively appeared in backstage segments, planking on crates and not uttering a word. That all changed on last week's SmackDown in his hometown of Cleveland.

In an effort to coax Gargano into getting up and getting back in the ring, WWE champion CM Punk offered to put the title on the line against Johnny Wrestling.

That was all Gargano needed, as he stood up and accepted Punk's challenge. They went on to have a spectacular match in the main event of the show, and Punk prevailed despite Sami Zayn interfering and attempting to cost Punk the title.

Last week marked Gargano's first match since competing in the Andre the Giant Memorial Battle Royal in April, so he figures to make up for lost time in the weeks and months to come.

Gargano has long been considered one of the best in-ring workers in pro wrestling, dating back to his time on the independent scene and in NXT.

There are plenty of exciting talents for Gargano to potentially work with on SmackDown, and last week seemingly opened the door to make that a reality.

Update on Jordynne Grace's Potential Return

Jordynne Grace has not wrestled a match on SmackDown since April, but her absence reportedly may be coming to an end soon.

Per Fightful Select (h/t Mrosko ), Grace may be slated to return to WWE programming in the near future, while doing something "categorically different" than she did previously.

A three-time TNA Knockouts world champion, Grace officially joined WWE in early 2025 as part of the NXT brand.

Although Grace never won the NXT Women's Championship, she was a key figure in the NXT women's division before getting quickly moved up to the main roster in January 2026.

Grace challenged Jade Cargill for the WWE Women's Championship about one month into her tenure on SmackDown, but after losing that match, she largely faded into the background.

While Grace has wrestled on Main Event a handful of times since her last SmackDown match against Tiffany Stratton in April, she has largely been out of sight and out of mind.

Grace is a big-time talent in the ring, though, and if WWE can figure out a good role for her on the blue brand, it should boost the women's division significantly.

articles.summary: Lachie Miller has been ruled out of Leeds Rhinos' play-offs campaign after he sustained a hamstring injury during his side's 40-8 defeat to Wigan Warriors; the regular Super League season concludes with Round 27 from Thursday September 10 live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Miller, who has been one of Leeds' most crucial attackers this season, sustained the injury during the early stages of his side's 40-8 defeat to Wigan Warriors on Saturday.

Arthur confirmed the news on Wednesday, adding the 32-year-old will not require surgery to remedy the injury.

It is a huge blow for Miller, who was a firm favourite to be crowned this season's Man of Steel, ranking third for the most metres and the most carries.

The Rhinos boss also revealed the surprising news that Ash Handley would step in at full-back for the injured Miller for his side's final regular-season Super League clash against Hull FC on Friday.

"He's going to avoid surgery, which is positive. But he's looking at 10 to 12 weeks," Arthur said.

"It's at the higher end of the scale, but it's not the highest because the next step would have been surgery.

"It's disappointing for his team-mates and the team, but I always put the player first. It's really disappointing for him because he's worked hard on things and done everything we've asked him to do.

"He was playing with a fractured eye socket going into the game. The plan was to get him through the Wigan game and the physios had a place saved for this Monday to have an operation if it got any worse."

articles.title: Anthony Edwards seems fired up about the Wolves' Jonathan Kuminga addition
articles.summary: Kuminga arrived in Minnesota on Tuesday and got a warm welcome from Edwards.
articles.body:
Jonathan Kuminga , the newest member of the Timberwolves , arrived in Minnesota for the first time on Tuesday, a couple weeks after spurning the Lakers and other teams to become the starting power forward the Wolves spent much of this offseason seeking.

According to multiple reports, including from Timberwolves insider Jon Krawczynski of The Athletic, Anthony Edwards was a big part of an organization-wide recruiting pitch that resulted in Kuminga choosing Minnesota. Edwards expressed his belief in the soon-to-be 24-year-old, who has been a bit of a polarizing figure during his time in the NBA so far. Ant also focused on selling Kuminga on what he could bring to the Wolves on the defensive end of the floor.

That context feels important when watching a new clip shared by the Timberwolves on Tuesday during Kuminga's first day in Minnesota. Edwards came to greet his new teammate with a trademark smile on his face.

"Y'all see what's going on," Edwards said. "This s*** over with, man. Wrap this s*** up."

In other words, Ant seems pretty confident in the Wolves' ceiling with Kuminga joining himself, LaMelo Ball , Jaden McDaniels , Rudy Gobert , Ayo Dosunmu , and the rest of a very intriguing roster that underwent a major offseason makeover.

The ultra-athletic, 6'7″ Kuminga has a chance to be a perfect fit for the Wolves as the final piece of their starting lineup puzzle. In order for that to be the case, he'll need to buy into his role . While playing with Edwards, Ball, and McDaniels, Kuminga can't expect to be a featured scorer who is going to play in isolation. He needs to focus on defense, rebounding, transition offensive, and connective passing.

The early indications are that Kuminga realizes as much . But we won't truly know how willing he is to embrace the dirty work until the games actually begin.

Kuminga will be introduced by the Timberwolves at a formal press conference on Thursday, according to reports. Those are sometimes reserved for more high-profile additions like Ball, but this could be viewed as another step in the Wolves making Kuminga feel valued after going all-out in recruiting him.

articles.title: Declan Doyle identifies three traits Ravens' offense must embody
articles.summary: Declan Doyle wants Baltimore’s new offense to be detailed, physical and explosive as the Ravens begin the season against Indianapolis.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens have enough talent to field one of the NFL's most dangerous offenses, but coordinator Declan Doyle wants the unit defined by more than its personnel. Doyle said he wants Baltimore's offense to be known for three qualities: being detailed, physical, and explosive.

Each trait will be essential as the Ravens transition to a new system built around Lamar Jackson . Details include proper alignment, timing, assignments, and communication. Baltimore cannot take full advantage of its talent if penalties, protection errors, or missed responsibilities repeatedly put the offense behind schedule.

Physicality should remain central to an attack featuring Jackson and Derrick Henry . Their presence forces defenses to account for multiple rushing threats on every snap, creating opportunities for play-action passes and favorable matchups downfield.

Explosiveness may ultimately determine the offense's ceiling. Jackson can create game-changing plays with his arm or legs, while Zay Flowers , Rashod Bateman and Baltimore's other playmakers give him multiple options in space.

Doyle first introduced those three nonnegotiable characteristics after accepting the position, and his message has remained consistent throughout the offseason. The Ravens' new coordinator has repeatedly emphasized physical, detailed, and explosive football as he installs his system. Baltimore's Week 1 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts will provide the first meaningful measurement of that vision. Doyle will call a regular-season NFL game for the first time, and the Ravens must execute the offense without exposing everything they plan to use during the season.

The personnel creates considerable potential, but talent alone will not establish Baltimore's identity. Doyle wants an offense that can punish defenses physically, avoid self-inflicted mistakes, and produce explosive plays from anywhere on the field.

articles.title: Solheim Cup: Yin faced a race against time to play for US after stomach issue. Now she's good to go
articles.summary: Angel Yin believes she’s ready to play the Solheim Cup.  Yin has been a big question mark for the Americans heading into this week’s matches against Team Eur...
articles.body:
DEN BOSCH, Netherlands (AP) — Angel Yin believes she's ready to play the Solheim Cup .

Just as importantly, so does her captain.

Yin has been a big question mark for the Americans heading into this week's matches against Team Europe in the Netherlands after missing two months with severe stomach issues and only returning for the final event before the Solheim Cup — where she shot 81-76 to miss the cut.

The 27-year-old Californian qualified automatically on the points list at No. 2 behind Nelly Korda for the Americans and, if in prime form, would be a go-to player for captain Angela Stanford as the U.S. team attempts to keep hold of the cup.

Yin thinks she can still be, despite her less-than-ideal preparation that has seen her lose 35 pounds and arrive at Bernardus Golf outside Den Bosch playing catch-up with her teammates and rivals.

"I wanted to be honest because I would never jeopardize America," Yin said Wednesday. "So I had honest talks with myself in the mirror and with my team, and obviously with Angela because she's the only other person, other than my family, that I've updated throughout all of this.

"And she wanted me here," Yin added. "Because we asked her ... well I didn't ask her, I had my caddie ask her, 'Do you want me here?' And if she said no, I wouldn't be here. But she said yes. So I think with belief like that and confidence from her to back me, why wouldn't I show up?"

Yin, who has dropped to No. 25 in the world, was out earlier than the rest of the U.S. team on Wednesday — when there was a mixture of rain, sunshine and clouds — in her quest for "more practice repetition."

She missed the year's last two majors after pulling out of the Women's PGA in the last week of June, and acknowledged her performance at the FM Championship in Boston two weeks ago — she was last in the field — was concerning.

"It's not a score you really bring out and you go, 'Wow, that's the person that's going to be helping America bring home the cup,'" she said.

Just don't expect Yin to be rolled out by Stanford for all five matches this week.

"I just need to wait for her call," she said, "and whatever she does and whatever she says will, in my opinion, be the best decision because we trust her, and she's been leading us great."

Trending in a different direction is U.S. teammate Rose Zhang, the one-time wonderkid who has found life on the professional tour tough after becoming, in June 2023, the first woman to win her pro debut since 1951.

Top-10 finishes in her last two starts hinted at a return to the kind of form that took her to a 4-0-0 record at the last Solheim Cup, won by the Americans in Virginia in 2024, and she has come to Europe on a high after going sky-diving last week.

Because what better way to prepare for the biggest event in women's golf?

"I didn't tell Angela this until after I jumped," Zhang said. "I should have just texted in the group chat, 'I landed.' But we were also joking about it the previous week in Boston that if one of the Europeans came and drove the plane, it would not be good," she added, laughing.

"It was extremely fun. I personally am a bit of an adrenaline junkie, and so I enjoy roller coasters, I'm not scared of heights. It just felt fitting to do it right before a Solheim."

articles.title: The Chip Kelly Offense — Charlie’s Film Room Week 1
articles.summary: Film Review is back baby!
articles.body:
The last time I had a film review piece come out was Jan. 15. It was a look at Aidan Chiles from the 2025 season after the news had broken that he was transferring to Evanston. It feels good to be back, plus I'm doing things a little differently (at least for this first one). Instead of having six to 10 clips all separate, I'm aiming to have multiple "B-Roll Blocks" of different aspects of the game, for example "Aidan Chiles passing" and then " Northwestern rushing." Also, the footage is now in all-22 format, which hopefully I'll be able to continue throughout the season. I also might not go through every single play in these cut-ups, but it's a good reference point. Every play I'll try to have two angles: the traditional all-22 view and the back view. With all that being said and out of the way, it's time to dive on in!

For his first game as a Wildcat, Chiles put some solid tape out there. His final stat line, 14-of-24 for 273 and one touchdown on 28 dropbacks, doesn't tell the full story of the tape. Chiles' EPA/play per PFF was 0.140, putting him right around the midpoint among all FBS quarterbacks that played in Weeks 0 and 1, including above Demond Williams Jr. ( Washington ), Micah Alejado ( Hawaii ), Drew Mestemaker (Oklahoma State) and Bryce Underwood ( Michigan ), just to name a few. Chiles did take two sacks, which is both on him and on the offensive line that was missing Ezomo Oratokhai and lost Jackson Carsello in the second half.

Chiles pushed the ball downfield often, only throwing two passes behind the line of scrimmage, while 13 of his throws were 10-plus yards downfield. On 20-plus yard throws, Chiles was 3-of-4 for 128. PFF considered Chiles to be under pressure on 11 of his dropbacks, during which he took the two sacks and was 4-of-7 for 113, compared to 10-of-17 for 160 and one touchdown without pressure. On the 10 play-action dropbacks, Chiles was 7-of-10 for 177, which included his first throw of the game to Griffin Wilde . On these 10 dropbacks, his EPA/play was 0.790 — 45th-highest in the FBS in Week 1.

Grant Seagren had the highest PFF offensive grade among Northwestern offensive linemen, but Anthony Birsa led the team in pass blocking grade after coming in for Carsello. Joseph Himon II and Gavin Sawchuk were sixth and eighth respectively in PFF rushing grade among Big Ten running backs this week, with Himon's 80-yard scamper contributing heavily to that. Wilde was the highest graded wide receiver for NU this week per PFF in both offensive and receiving grades, running 28 routes on 29 pass snaps and going 3-for-104. Interestingly enough, Northwestern only played four wide receivers in this game: Wilde, Hayden Eligon II, Drew Wagner and Ricky Ahumaraeze. Something that popped out of the stats is that Wagner led the team in targets (and it wasn't particularly close). Wagner was targeted seven times, with Wilde's four targets being the second-most for NU.

Alex Honig had the highest receiving grade of any Northwestern player (seventh in Big Ten), finishing with the lone receiving touchdown. He ran six routes on eight pass snaps, with Luke Dehnicke being the more featured tight end in the receiving game. The Division II transfer ran 23 routes on 25 pass snaps: the third-most routes run for NU behind Wilde and Wagner. Dehnicke was also targeted twice, finishing 2-for-41 but flashing his potential in this Chip Kelly offense.

On the first offensive play for Northwestern in Kelly's offense, Chiles hit Wilde off the play-action fake for a massive gain. What's most impressive is Chiles' pocket awareness, stepping up and delivering the throw with defenders encircling him. South Dakota State sent five rushers, and Chiles is able to read the cover 2 look, with one of the safeties slipping to allow for the massive gain. The very next play, Chiles works through his progressions to find Honig who is sitting in a soft spot of the cover 3 defense for an easy touchdown. Deuce McGuire also took the left edge rusher completely out of the play.

In the next clip, Chiles showcases his ability to extend plays with his legs. While his pocket passing was fairly good in this game, part of the appeal to his game is his athleticism with his legs and his potential to improvise. The play-action fake drags No. 97 away from Chiles, who jukes a defender before an easy dump-off to Honig. The levels concept in this play worked on both levels, with Eligon II also open, although Chiles chose to go with the easier throw while on the run against what looks to be a disguised fire zone 3 blitz. For the next clip, although it's a check down, it shows Chiles' ability to maneuver the pocket. The Jackrabbits play cover 1 man on this play, but Komolafe goes unmarked and Chiles finds him after going through his progressions and failing to find an open man. McGuire again does a great job keeping Chiles clean on his right side.

After Carsello went down with a neck injury, Birsa held up fantastically at center, which can be seen in this next clip. Chiles diagnoses what looks to be a Tampa 2 defense and finds Drew Wagner right in that sweet spot of the zone up the right seam for a big gain, despite Tampa 2 not being the easiest defense to throw up the seam on. The play after, South Dakota State shows Chiles a cover 3 look, which he dices up perfectly by hitting Dehnicke in the right seam for another big gain. This rep was also one of the more cleaner ones for the offensive line, with it looking like Chiles could have stayed in the pocket for another second or two. On the final clip in this cut-up, the Jackrabbits send six at Chiles and play man in the backend. Chiles stands in the pocket and delivers a strike right in the bucket to Wagner just in front of the defender. It was a great grab by Wagner and a money throw from Chiles.

This is just one clip, and it's Chiles' rushing touchdown. There's not much to diagnose on Chiles' part in this play, but I still wanted to include it to show off the play design. Northwestern is in 12 personnel here with just a yard to gain on third-and-1, and Chiles fakes the sneak and takes it around the left side untouched into the end zone, catching South Dakota State sleeping.

Northwestern has three running backs that undoubtedly will make an impact this season, and that was showcased immediately. Eye test wise, Sawchuk looked the best on the ground overall, Komolafe showed his ability to fight through contact and Himon II showed off his explosiveness. Komolafe led with 10 carries, followed by Sawchuk with eight and Himon II with four. While Himon II's 21.8 yards-per-carry average is ballooned by his long rushing touchdown, he showed his ability as a home-run hitter and his prowess after he breaks into the open field. He also caught a pass for 15 yards, where the same thing was on display. In these clips, Sawchuk's ability to wait and follow his blockers to diagnose his running lanes is very impressive. His patience combined with his shiftiness allowed for him to average 8.6 yards per carry despite his longest run being 21 yards. Take away that run, and he still would have averaged just about 4.6 yards a pop. Komolafe did average 4.6 yards per carry across his 10 attempts, plus he added 37 yards on two receptions. Komolafe ran more routes than Himon II in this game, which could be a sign of things to come with him as a multi-dimensional back. Komolafe's final rushing total was 46 yards. Forty of those yards came after contact. AFTER CONTACT! He had the same amount of rush yards after contact as Darius Taylor did this week, who himself had three rushing scores against a much weaker Eastern Illinois defense. All three backs showcased their respective games and how they can be involved in this offense, with all providing something a bit different to create a murky situation for fantasy football, but an offensive coordinator's dream for mixing up personnel.

articles.title: Why Jeff Hafley should keep it simple with these young Dolphins
articles.summary: What the NFL's youngest roster needs from Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley
articles.body:
MIAMI GARDENS ― During the preseason, including joint practices, Miami Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley was open about keeping schemes simple.

The key, Hafley explained, was getting a complete evaluation of the players.

It was not about tricking opponents with complex strategies.

It's my opinion that Hafley should take a similar approach in the regular season, starting with the season-opener at Las Vegas on Sunday, Sept. 13.

Keep it simple. Less complex. Limit risk.

Recently I asked Hafley about if he'll use his "gut" to potentially override some in-game recommendations from the analytics teams, such as punting or going for it on fourth down.

"I think you have a plan, and I think a lot of the times you try to stick with your plan, but there's always got to be the feel of the game and where it's going and the momentum of the game and how I think everything is going and what the team needs from me right now," Hafley said.

Much of the strategy will be determined the week before the game. Stick with the plan.

Miami is currently an underdog in 16 of 17 regular-season games. But the Dolphins have a shot on Sunday.

Photos of Miami Dolphins 53-man roster - until they add/drop players

Miami Dolphins roster is youngest in NFL

They're only 3.5-point underdogs and facing a beatable quarterback, Kirk Cousins .

If rookie Fernando Mendoza was making his first career start, it might make more sense to throw a few "kitchen sinks" at the youngster.

But Cousins has seen everything. There is no need to throw a bunch of blitzes at him that may confuse Miami's 14-member rookie class more than Cousins.

Keep it simple. Give the team a chance. Help limit busts from a very inexperienced secondary.

Blowouts can be demoralizing for a young group. Limiting blowouts could prove beneficial in the long-run.

Go for it on 4th-and-1 from Miami's 39-yard line on the first possession of the season?

We say punt. And that hurts to write. But punt.

Limit short fields for the defense. Limit tons of snaps for the defense. This team lacks depth.

Dolphins could play it conservative early on

Hafley noted he was among the leaders in going for it on fourth down at Boston College one season.

At times, BC was undermanned in a manner similar to what the Dolphins figure to face this year.

The goal this season is to, yes, try to win some games. But even more important is to evaluation of players, particularly young players.

Former Dolphins coach Dave Wannstedt, a mentor of Hafley's, used to say in so many words that the punt is not a bad play (certainly compared to a turnover on downs, interception or lost fumble).

Times have changed. Far more teams now are going for it on 4th-and-1.

But tapping into some of Wannstedt's mindset this season would not be the worst thing.

Could Miami roll out an exotic blitz here or later there this season?

Sure. But starting out "base" and "vanilla" seems the best way to go early in the season.

"I'm going to call what I believe our guys can execute at a high level," Hafley said, a few days before the opener.

Miami needs to evaluate their players in 1-on-1 situations this season. It's far less essential to scheme up free runners or 2-on-1's. Evaluation must be key to every decision.

Miami Dolphins ' Jeff Hafley could keep it vanilla early on

Miami has the youngest roster in the league. Keep it simple.

I once asked a college coach about how fast a young player was.

"That's great but if you're running the wrong way, you just get there faster," he said.

Miami figures to have some rookies running fast, but the wrong way on Sunday.

Keep it simple. Limit mistakes. Just play fast and free.

articles.title: England demolish Pakistan to take charge of Test
articles.summary: England again demolish the dismal Pakistan batting to move on course for a 3-0 clean sweep on the opening day of the third Test at Edgbaston.
articles.body:
Third Rothesay Test, Edgbaston (day one of five)

Pakistan 133: Shakeel 43; Tongue 4-42, Robinson 3-15, Archer 3-25

England again demolished the dismal Pakistan batting to move on course for a 3-0 clean sweep on the opening day of the third Test at Edgbaston.

After ripping out the tourists for only 133, England already have an 23-run advantage on 156-4.

Following a week of turmoil in which Pakistan sent seven players home, called up seven more and changed their coach, the outcome was much the same as the first two Tests.

Though the dry pitch seemed good for batting, a moody morning sky convinced England captain Joe Root to field first and his new-look pace attack was outstanding once more.

Pakistan failed to reach 200 for the fifth consecutive innings, while none of the top five made double figures. Saud Shakeel at least managed 43 and the ineptitude of the top order was put into context by last-wicket pair Muhammad Abbas and Mohammad Ali adding 26 in 46 balls - the best partnership of the innings.

Josh Tongue bowled quickly for his 4-42, Ollie Robinson passed 100 Test wickets with his 3-15 and Jofra Archer claimed the remaining three scalps.

In truth, it was a disappointing and dispiriting spectacle, but Pakistan showed some fight with the ball, not least when rapid debutant Razaullah inflicted yet another lbw on Root to leave England 39-3.

Emilio Gay and Harry Brook steadied England, each making half-centuries in a stand of 104 that pushed the hosts into the lead.

Gay dragged on off Razaullah. His gritty 60 was impressive, if perhaps not enough to provide certainty around his place in a congested England batting line-up.

Pakistan changes fail to alter one-sided contest

The pattern of this day was entirely predictable from the moment Root won the toss and there were times in the early going when the action was neither elite sport nor satisfying entertainment.

The conditions for a Test played in September were autumnal and one side of Edgbaston is a building site. Some 15,000 tickets were sold for today, yet the ground was not half-full when play began. The atmosphere was flat.

Pakistan made four changes from the second Test at Lord's, including three debutants. England, as expected, resisted tinkering with their attack and the hosts had the Pakistan innings wrapped up in 33.5 overs.

At least Pakistan landed some blows on the England top-order. Ben Duckett and Jordan Cox played loose shots - potentially costly for Cox as he looks to nail down his place - and Root was lbw for the 10th time in 13 innings in Razaullah's first over in Test cricket.

Gay and Brook restored order in the evening sunshine and it already seems certain England will win before the weekend. It could even be over inside two days.

Quite what Root's developing England team can take from this series is unclear. The disparity between the two sides in these conditions is simply too large.

Gay has had the entire summer to make the opening position his own, though the arrivals of Cox and Dan Lawrence could make him most vulnerable when Jacob Bethell returns from a knee injury.

But Gay has been batting in the hardest position at a time when all batters have struggled for runs. This knock, in an innings when Cox wasted his chance, did his cause no harm without being a compelling case for long-term retention.

The Durham man was patient and watchful and also came through moments of frantic running with Brook. When the opportunity arose, the left-hander scored with handsome strokes through the off side.

Brook arrived when Razaullah was pushing the speed gun, and the England vice-captain also had to battle his recent weakness with the wicketkeeper standing up.

The fourth-wicket pair gradually halted Pakistan's brief spell of momentum, taking England ahead.

For Gay, a third half-century in six Tests came from 95 deliveries. Reaching the close unbeaten would have presented a golden opportunity for a big score on Thursday, only for a limp prod at Razaullah to leave more questions and a sense of what might have been.

Robinson began this summer in an exile from the England team that had lasted for more than two years. He ends it as the attack leader, with statistics that stack up alongside some of the all-time greats of the game.

He had already had one lbw decision against Saim Ayub overturned by the time he pinned the same batter again in his second over. It gave Robinson his 100th Test wicket at an average of 19.34 - the first England bowler since Ian Botham to reach 100 wickets at an average below 20.

Indeed, no bowler since World War II with at least 100 Test wickets has a better average than Robinson. His three on Wednesday gave him a total of 27 for the summer at a cost of 7.96 apiece.

Such was their dominance, England could afford Duckett to miss two tough chances at first slip. Root, often captaining from short leg, set fields that crowded the bat, often with seven catchers.

Tongue bowled with high pace and targeted the stumps – all four of his wickets were bowled or lbw. Archer benefitted from two miscues from mid-on, then came back to eventually end the Ali-Abbas last-wicket stand.

The curiosity is Gus Atkinson. He has not bowled badly, yet has somehow missed out on the riches of his fellow seamers. While the rest have cleaned up, Atkinson has just one wicket in the series at an average of 156.

articles.title: Zac Taylor provides latest update on Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins
articles.summary: Bengals coach Zac Taylor said on Sept. 9 that his star wide receivers are progressing ahead of the Sept. 13 home opener against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
articles.body:
Cincinnati Bengals coach Zac Taylor said on Sept. 9 that his star wide receivers are progressing ahead of the Sept. 13 home opener against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers .

Taylor said Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins were working toward being full participants in practice , after the duo returned to practice on Sept. 7.

Taylor also updated the status of second-year defensive end Shemar Stewart , but didn't predict if he'd play this week. "We'll progress him this week and see how it ends up," Taylor said.

The Bengals and Buccaneers are scheduled for a 1 p.m. kickoff at Paycor Stadium and the game will be broadcast on Fox19.

articles.title: Carse & McKinney put Durham on top against Middlesex
articles.summary: Brydon Carse's five-wicket haul and Ben McKinney's century put Division Two leaders Durham in control against Middlesex.
articles.body:
Rothesay County Championship, Division Two, Banks Homes Riverside (day two)

Durham 252: Raine 58*; Morgan 4-78, Sharma 3- 38, Higgins 3-63 & 204-2 McKinney 115*

Middlesex 203: Holden 43, Duke 38*; Carse 5-72, Raine 3-67

Durham (4 pts) lead Middlesex (3 pts) by 253 runs

Brydon Carse's first five-wicket haul in almost two years and a sublime century from Ben McKinney helped promotion-chasing Durham take control of their Division Two clash with Middlesex.

The visitors made a good start to the day, as they saw out a challenging opening hour with the bat. Durham then struck back with four wickets in the second half of the morning session, with Ben Raine taking two of them.

The hosts picked up where they left off after lunch and Carse wrapped up the tail to secure his first five-for in any form of cricket since taking 6-42 in a Test match against New Zealand in 2024.

It was also his first County Championship five-wicket haul since 2021 and saw Middlesex bowled out for 203, a deficit of 49.

Division Two front-runners Durham then took the upper hand in this match as they made an excellent start to their second innings, Alex Lees and McKinney combining for an opening stand worth 81. McKinney then passed three figures and Durham closed on 204-2, leading by 253 runs.

Durham's performance on the second day has given them a platform to win the game, a result which would seal their return to Division One, while Middlesex have plenty of work to do if they are to take something from their visit to the North East.

Resuming on 70-2, Middlesex's Nathan Fernandes and Max Holden chipped away at Durham's lead in the first half-hour, with conditions challenging for batting.

The pair's partnership passed 50 before Kasey Aldridge made the breakthrough, as he removed Holden, who could only edge an attempted drive straight to third slip. Durham got their fourth wicket soon after, as Will Rhodes made a mess of Fernandes' stumps.

Raine got Durham's fifth when Ben Geddes edged to Colin Ackermann at second slip, and claimed another on the stroke of lunch, as Ryan Higgins sent one straight to first slip.

The hosts continued where they left off after the break, with Raine getting Zafar Gohar lbw.

Carse then got his third of the innings as he trapped Seb Morgan lbw for a duck. Harry Duke and Tom Helm frustrated Durham with a 40-run partnership but Carse had Helm caught behind.

The England bowler then wrapped up the innings as he got Naavya Sharma lbw, with the hosts securing a 49-run first innings lead.

Lees and McKinney got Durham's second innings off to a solid start, with the pair finding the boundary at regular intervals.

The Durham openers notched up their 50 partnership and continued to build their lead as it passed three figures. Lees then fell as he was bowled by Higgins, but McKinney continued his good start as he reached 50.

Rhodes joined McKinney at the crease and looked assured with a lovely cut shot bringing up the pair's 50 partnership.

McKinney continued to look good in the middle, scoring heavily through the off side, and the left-handed opener helped his team extend their lead past 200.

Middlesex hit back when Rhodes was caught at gully off the bowling of Morgan, but that didn't stop McKinney making his third century of the summer and he got there in style with a lovely shot through the covers.

Mayank Agarwal joined McKinney at the crease and the pair saw their side through to close without further loss as bad light brought an early end to the day.

articles.title: Dylan Lonergan Will Not Start For Rutgers: Will He Play At All In Return?
articles.summary: The former Eagles QB left the season-opener with an injury.
articles.body:
The stage was set for Dylan Lonergan to make his return to Chestnut Hill early in the 2026 season.

Instead, Lonergan was removed with an injury during Rutgers ' 37-21 season-opening loss to UMass on Thursday night.

Earlier in the week, Rutgers head coach Greg Schiano announced that AJ Surace would start on Friday against Boston College after Lonergan was unable to practice.

Right now, we know that Lonergan will not start the game but it will be interesting to see if he plays at all, if active. We will not know this answer until the injury report comes out before kick off.

During his game week press conference, Eagles' head coach Bill O'Brien spoke on Lonergan.

"Dylan's a really good player," O'Brien said. "I've said that before. I think I said that a couple weeks ago or whenever you guys asked me about that last. Excellent quarterback. Very smart. I think he's got a really, really talented arm. Very competitive and, you know, it's gonna be a big challenge for us."

Lonergan went 16-for-29 for 242 yards with two touchdowns and three interceptions before being removed in the fourth quarter.

Boston College will host Rutgers in the Red Bandana game on Friday night at 7:30pm from Alumni Stadium in Chestnut Hill.

articles.title: Trenches Preview: Arizona State at Texas A&M
articles.summary: Talking offfensive and defensive lines as Texas A&M hosts Arizona State in P4 non-conference action
articles.body:
Texas A&M kicked off the 2026 season with a dominant 50-0 win over Missouri State. Still, this contest didn't come without hiccups, some of which took place in the trenches. The Aggies will need a better effort come Saturday to defeat a hungry Arizona State squad. Let's talk about what needs to happen in the trenches for Texas A&M to come out on top.

The Aggies did win up front last Saturday, but it wasn't as dominant as you would like, especially in the first half. Some of the issues we expected with twists and stunts up front did cause problems for Texas A&M. The problem was most obvious on a drive where Marcel Reeed took two sacks in a row. Additionally, of the eight penalties Texas A&M had against the Bears, four were called against the offensive line. Mike Elko called the penalty situation better than last year's, noting that they weren't lazy penalties, but penalties kill drives, and Texas A&M can't afford that against better competition.

In Arizona State, Texas A&M faces an experienced foe up front. The Sun Devil defensive line features upperclassmen at all four positions across the two-deep. Defensive end Jalen Thompson, in particular, looked disruptive against Morgan State in ASU's 70-0 win. However, given the level of competition, it's hard to draw any real conclusions about the talent Arizona State has up front. One thing I did notice that will be relevant for this weekend, however, was Arizona State defensive coordinator Brian Ward's penchant for exotics. The Texas A&M offensive line was better at communicating in the second half, but they will need to prove they can do it for a complete game against Arizona State.

I do expect the offense to open the playbook up a bit, which could help the offensive line as well, but I'm expecting more early-season struggles against the Sun Devils.

On the other side of the ball, the Texas A&M defensive line did exactly what was expected of them against Missouri State. The Aggies limited the Bears to just 67 total yards on the day, sacking Skyler Locklear once and tacking on six tackles for loss. Missouri State ran for just 37 yards on 23 carries, averaging 1.6 YPC. Again, given the level of competition, we can't really draw a hard conclusion on this trench unit just yet, but the Aggies looked disciplined and disruptive barring one questionable roughing the passer call against Anto Saka. The quick game of Missouri State and the scramble ability of Locklear didn't allow a ton of chances for Texas A&M to pin their ears back but in the brief glimpses of Ryan Henderson we saw, it looks like the Aggies have another pass-rushing threat to go along with the trinity of T.J. Searcy, Marco Jones, and Anto Saka.

That pass rush will be necessary against an Arizona State passing attack led by Cutter Boley. The Sun Devils lit up Morgan State, but, to beat a dead horse, the level of competition is dramatically different than what to expect against the Aggies. Boley threw for 387 yards and six touchdowns. I expect a bit more traditional drop-back passing game from Arizona State on Saturday, giving the Aggies more chances to rush the passer. Boley isn't the threat to scramble that Locklear was either, giving the defensive line a bit more freedom to get creative in their rushes. Morgan State did have two sacks against Arizona State, so the potential to pressure Boley into mistakes certainly exists against this offensive line, which, much like Texas A&M, features a lot of new faces. The Aggies will need to be wary of backs releasing out of the backfield, as Grayson Rigdon went for 110 yards and two touchdowns on just two catches.

The Sun Devils also ran for 249 yards on 35 carries. Of note in the rushing attack was that no running back had double-digit rushing attempts. Senior Kyson Brown is listed as the starter and led the Sun Devils in rushing yards and attempts against Morgan State, but the Aggies can expect a healthy rotation. Texas A&M will need to keep the gap discipline that was shown on Saturday, allowing Noah Mikhail to filter and make plays. Perhaps the biggest question is whether Daymion Sanford will be back in the fold for Arizona State after sitting against Missouri State. The changing linebacker rotation could impact how the Aggies approach Saturday's contest up front.

Arizona State should provide a solid early-season mental check for Texas A&M, and if the Aggies aren't prepared, they could wind up with the first loss of 2026. Ultimately, I do think the Aggies will come out on top, but don't expect this to be an easy game. I have Texas A&M winning 24-14.
